newsitem.title: POLAND: Daewoo to invest $2.2 bln in Polish units in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo to invest $2.2 bln in Polish units in 5 yrs.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo plans to invest a total of $2.215 billion in the automotive industry in Poland by the year 2001, the Polish Daewoo-FSO car plant's financial head told a news conference on Tuesday.
"Until 2001 we want to invest $2.215 billion in three already operating companies as well as a network of firms and branches," Janusz Lach said.
He said investment in Daewoo's plant in the south-eastern twon of Lublin would total $500 million by 2001 and another $215 million in the engine plant Andoria in the town of Andrychow.
Maciej Motelski, head of Daewoo-FSO's production, said that until 2001 investment in the Daewoo-FSO plant in Warsaw would total $1.5 billion of which one third would be spent in 1996-1997.
"We want to produce 500,000 cars anually in Daewoo-FSO. Investment in 1996 and 1997 will total $507 million," he said.
Lach said that under the investment programme Daewoo would start assembling a new car model called Lanos in September 1997 and start fully producing it in Poland in March 1998.
He said that in October 1997 the company would start assembling the Laganza model and that it would also introduce a third model, Nubira, at an unspecified date.
He said Daewoo planned to produce a total of 550,000 cars in Poland by 2001 of which 100,000 would be the Polonez and Polonez Truck models and 200,000 cars would go for exports.
"In exports we want to concentrate on the Truck model, especially for the Asian and South American markets. In the case of new models it will be Europe and North Africa," Lach said.
